name: Merlin 1D (sea level)
used_on: Falcon 9 first stage (9 engines), Falcon Heavy (27)
notes: Gas-generator kerosene engine, 9.7 MPa chamber pressure. Bell exit shown at 0.92 m, the engine diameter on Wikipedia. The 3D model is a light (4k-face) Merlin by hoahluke, not an exact CAD copy. Wikipedia tags the Isp figures as needing an update and sources the dry mass to a non-SpaceX answer.

name: Merlin 1D Vacuum
used_on: Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy second stage (1 engine)
notes: Merlin 1D with a long radiatively cooled niobium nozzle extension (165:1 expansion). Bell exit shown at 2.4 m (the figure used in the lab brief; it also makes the model's proportions come out at about 4.1 m long). Wikipedia lists a 3.3 m overall diameter for the vacuum engine, which may include the nozzle extension at full width, so treat the exit size as approximate. The same page lists 311 s in its infobox and 348 s in the text (shown: 348 s).

name: Raptor (Raptor 2 class)
used_on: Super Heavy (33 engines), Starship (3 sea-level + 3 vacuum)
notes: Sea-level Raptor 2: 2,256 kN, 347 s, length 3.1 m, 1,630 kg (Wikipedia). The 1.3 m bell exit is the original 2018 design figure; Wikipedia gives no measured Raptor 2 exit diameter. The 3D model is a Raptor of unspecified revision by MartianDays. The vacuum variant (about 2,530 kN) has a 2.4 m class nozzle and is not modelled separately.

name: Rocketdyne J-2S
used_on: never flown; the J-2 it derives from flew on Saturn V S-II (5) and S-IVB (1), Saturn IB S-IVB
notes: Simplified J-2 (tap-off cycle, no gas generator) test-fired 1965-1972 and cancelled; considered for the Shuttle and the Comet HLLV. 3.38 m long, about 2 m across (Wikipedia gives 2.01 m as the engine diameter). The Shipyard uses this model for the J-2 engines of Saturn V S-II and S-IVB, which look near-identical from outside.

name: Generic bell engine
notes: Library model of an unspecified bell engine ('Rocket Engine' by ~Drift~). Not a real engine: no performance figures, and the bell exit is set to an arbitrary 1 m so it can be viewed. Not placed on any vehicle in the labs.
